Hotel Equities Earns Fourth Consecutive #1 Ranking as Marriott’s Top Performing Franchise Management Company Based on Intent to Recommend (ITR) Scores 

### Hotel Equities Earns Fourth Consecutive #1 Ranking as Marriott’s Top Performing Franchise Management Company Based on Intent to Recommend (ITR) Scores 

 August 14, 2026 

ATLANTA, GA – Hotel Equities (“HE”), a best-in-class hospitality operator and developer, has once again earned the #1 ranking as Marriott’s Top Performing Franchise Management Company (FMC) in the U.S. and Canada for Q2 2026 among management companies operating 51 or more Marriott Select Brand (MSB) hotels, based on Intent to Recommend (ITR) scores.

The latest recognition marks Hotel Equities’ fourth consecutive time earning the #1 ranking, demonstrating sustained leadership in one of Marriott’s most important measures of guest satisfaction and loyalty.

The achievement carries even greater significance for hotel owners following Marriott International’s recent announcement of a new ITR incentive program designed to financially reward eligible hotels that achieve strong guest satisfaction scores. Under the program, qualifying hotels may receive rebates of up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue, funded directly from Marriott’s profit and loss statement rather than shared system funds.

“ITR has always been more than a guest satisfaction score for us,” said David Rosenberg, President, Focused Service Division for HE. “It’s an operating metric that tells us whether we’re getting the fundamentals right at the hotel level. Now, with Marriott putting a direct financial incentive behind ITR performance, the connection between the guest experience and owner returns is even more tangible. For owners, that makes consistent execution incredibly important. Earning the number-one ranking four consecutive times across a portfolio of our size demonstrates that our results are repeatable and scalable, not isolated to a handful of high-performing hotels. We’ve built the systems, accountability and operating discipline to keep ITR at the forefront, and our teams understand that every guest interaction ultimately contributes to the performance and value of the asset.”

With ITR performance now carrying an even more direct financial benefit for qualifying owners, a management company’s ability to consistently drive guest satisfaction has never been more consequential.

Intent to Recommend, or ITR, is a key Marriott performance measure reflecting guest loyalty, satisfaction and brand advocacy. Hotel Equities’ sustained leadership in ITR reflects the company’s commitment to operational excellence and its ability to translate a people-first culture into measurable performance across a large and diverse portfolio.

### Hotel Equities Earns Top Honors in Marriott International’s Q1 2026 Performance Results based on Intent to Recommend (ITR) Scores

ATLANTA, GA – Hotel Equities (“HE”), a best-in-class hospitality operator and developer, has once again been recognized by Marriott International for outstanding performance, earning top distinctions across multiple categories in the global brand’s Q1 2026 results.

Among the achievements, Hotel Equities earned the #1 Top Performing Management Company in the United States and Canada for Marriott Select Brand Hotels, based on Intent to Recommend (ITR) scores, a key measure of guest loyalty, satisfaction, and brand advocacy.

What Is Marriott Intent to Recommend, or ITR?

Intent to Recommend, commonly abbreviated as ITR, is a Marriott performance measure of guest loyalty, satisfaction and brand advocacy.

Further demonstrating the strength and breadth of its operating platform, Hotel Equities was also recognized as the #3 Top Performing Management Company in the United States and Canada for Marriott Premium & Luxury Hotels, based on Intent to Recommend scores.

In Canada, Hotel Equities earned distinction as the Top Performing Management Company, based on Marriott’s Topline Activator scores, a metric that reflects strong revenue performance, market share growth, and operational effectiveness across the portfolio.

“These results are only achieved through the dedication of our hotel teams and the consistency with which they deliver exceptional guest experiences across every segment of our portfolio,” said Peter Tziahanas, President, Full Service Division. “To be recognized by Marriott for outstanding guest satisfaction across Select, Premium & Luxury brands, while also leading the Canadian market in topline performance, displays the strength of our people, our operating disciplines, and our commitment to creating value for our owners, guests, and brand partners.”

Marriott’s quarterly performance rankings are a benchmark for hospitality excellence within the industry, measuring both guest satisfaction and commercial performance across management companies throughout North America.

Hotel Equities’ continued recognition reinforces the company’s reputation for operational discipline, strong owner returns, and a purpose-driven culture that consistently drives results across a diverse portfolio of hotels.

### Hotel Equities Earns Top Honors in Marriott International’s Q4 2025 Performance Results 

 February 13, 2026 

Hotel Equities (“HE”), a best-in-class hospitality operator and developer, has once again been recognized by Marriott International for exceptional performance, earning top distinctions in the global brand’s Q4 2025 results. 

Among the achievements, Hotel Equities earned the #1 Top Performing Franchise Management Company based on Intent to Recommend scores for companies operating 51+ Marriott International Select Brand hotels across the United States and Canada — a key indicator of guest loyalty and brand advocacy.

Hotel Equities was also recognized among the Top 5 Performing Franchise Management Companies in Canada for Topline Activator Scores, reflecting strong revenue performance, market leadership, and disciplined operational strategy across its Canadian portfolio.

In addition, Postcard Cabins Gilchrest Spring, Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy, ranked among the Top 10 Performing Franchised Hotels in the United States. Notably, this marks the first time a property within Marriott International’s new Outdoor Collection has earned a spot on the Top Performer list — a milestone achievement for both the brand and Hotel Equities.

“From guest satisfaction to topline performance, these results demonstrate the strength of our operating culture and our commitment to delivering consistent excellence for our owners, brand partners, and guests,” said Al Smith, Chief Operating Officer of Hotel Equities.

Marriott’s quarterly performance metrics are widely regarded as a reliable benchmark for evaluating operational effectiveness and financial performance at scale. ### Hotel Equities Named as a Top Performing Franchise Management Company for Premium & Luxury Hotels by Marriott International, Recognized for Exceptional Guest Satisfaction 

 September 04, 2025 

Hotel Equities (“HE”), a best-in-class hospitality operator and developer, today announced it has been recognized by Marriott International as a Top Performing Franchise Management Company in the United States and Canada for Premium & Luxury hotels for the second quarter of 2025. The recognition is based on leading Intent to Recommend (ITR) scores among hotel management companies operating 8+ Premium & Luxury hotels. ITR is a measure of guest satisfaction across Marriott’s portfolio. 

In addition to the overall company achievement, The Farnam, Autograph Collection in Omaha, Nebraska, from Hotel Equities’ managed portfolio, earned recognition among Marriott’s Top 5 Performing Franchised Premium & Luxury Hotels. 

“Our differentiator is the attention to detail that our associates deliver each and every day, and our guests notice and appreciate,” said Al Smith, chief operating officer of Hotel Equities. “I want to congratulate and express my gratitude to the leaders across our organization who set the standard in excellence and consistently prioritize guest satisfaction and comfort as the baseline of true hospitality. These recognitions reflect the passion, precision, and care our entire organization delivers on behalf of our owners and partners.” 

Two of Hotel Equities’ select service properties in Canada, the TownePlace Suites by Marriott Medicine Hat in Alberta and the TownePlace Suites by Marriott Belleville in Ontario, were also recognized as Top Performers for ITR scores. 

Marriott’s performance metrics, including ITR scores, are vital indicators of a management company’s ability to deliver best-in-class guest satisfaction and financial performance. Hotel Equities’ consistent recognition across multiple categories highlights its proven success in optimizing hotel operations, elevating guest loyalty, and maximizing asset value for ownership groups.

Hotel Equities Named Top Performer by Marriott for Intent to Recommend in 4th Quarter 2023 

### Hotel Equities Named Top Performer by Marriott for Intent to Recommend in 4th Quarter 2023 

 February 12, 2024 

Today, Hotel Equities (“HE”), a leading hospitality management and development company, proudly announced its recognition by Marriott as the Top Performer for Intent to Recommend for franchise management companies operating 50+ Marriott Select Brand hotels in the United States for the 4th Quarter of 2023. 

 The acknowledgment reinforces HE’s commitment to its founding mission to make a distinct difference in people’s lives, a sentiment delivered through creating exceptional guest experiences and maintaining high standards across its entire portfolio of properties. The achievement reflects the dedication and hard work of the entire Hotel Equities team in consistently exceeding guest expectations and driving satisfaction. 

 Al Smith, President of Hotel Operations at HE, expressed his gratitude for the recognition, stating, "We are honored to receive this acknowledgement from Marriott. It is a testament to the dedication of our team members who continually go above and beyond to ensure the satisfaction of our guests. This achievement reaffirms our team’s passion to serve and motivates us to continue raising the bar." 

 The recognition holds special significance for HE, as its Founder and Chairman, Fred Cerrone, was among Marriott's initial franchise partners. His legacy underscores the company's deeprooted commitment to upholding Marriott's vision and values, aligned with his own vision for excellence. 

 "This recognition doubles down on our commitment to growth with quality,” said James Hansen, EVP of Business Development for HE. “We are determined to continue expanding our portfolio while prioritizing unparalleled guest experiences, ensuring that every property we manage exceeds expectations and delivers exceptional service." 

HE manages a diverse portfolio of best-in-class select- and full-service properties across North America to include Marriott, Hilton, IHG and Hyatt brands.

# What If Guest Satisfaction Became A Line On The Hotel P&L? | Onboard XP · LinkedIn · 2026-08-24

**Onboard XP**: Onboard XP is a company that designs, develops, and supplies smart, sustainable, and desirable products for the travel experience of guests, passengers, and employees. They offer a wide range of products including dining, comfort, relaxation, cleaning, entertainment, and serving products. They believe in a future of smart, sustainable products that do not compromise on quality or aesthetics. Onboard XP has 1-10 employees, founded in 2016. Headquartered in Los Angeles, California, United States, with an office in Redmond. Its workforce is distributed across United States and China.

---

What If Guest Satisfaction Became A Line On The Hotel P&L?

For years, hospitality has measured guest satisfaction.

Survey it.
Score it.
Benchmark it.
Report it.

Marriott is taking the relationship between guest experience and hotel economics one step further.

The company is introducing a financial incentive tied to Intent to Recommend — ITR — one of its key guest-satisfaction measures.

For eligible hotels in the U.S. and Canada that reach defined ITR thresholds, Marriott says the incentive can provide fee reimbursement worth up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue.

Read that again.

A guest-experience metric can now influence hotel-owner economics.

GUEST EXPERIENCE
→ INTENT TO RECOMMEND
→ PERFORMANCE THRESHOLD
→ FEE REIMBURSEMENT
→ OWNER ECONOMICS.

That is bigger than another satisfaction score.

Hospitality has spent decades trying to prove something operators intuitively understand:

Better guest experience should create business value.

Usually, that value appears indirectly.

The guest returns.

The guest spends more.

The guest recommends the hotel.

Reputation strengthens.

Demand follows.

But Marriott is creating something more explicit:

A mechanism connecting measured guest satisfaction to an economic outcome for qualifying hotels.

Hotel Equities recently ranked #1 among Marriott Select Brand franchise management companies with 51+ hotels for ITR performance for the fourth consecutive period.

But the ranking isn't the real story.

The real story is what happens when experience enters the financial architecture of hospitality.

At Onboard XP, we believe guest experience becomes strategically different when an organization stops treating it only as a score —

and starts connecting it to the economics of the asset.

Because behind an ITR number is not simply data.

There was a guest.

A room that was ready — or wasn't.

A problem that was solved — or wasn't.

A human interaction that felt exceptional — or forgettable.

Those moments eventually become a metric.

And now that metric can carry an economic consequence.

That changes the conversation.

Guest experience is no longer sitting beside the business model.

It is entering the business model.
